decision_question: Were the 16 source-semantic-atom failures genuine product defects, evaluator false positives, or invalid reference questions, and do they justify changing the frozen release gates?

hard_gates.name: prior-result-immutability
hard_gates.evidence: The official result, metrics, gates, responses, and source packages were hash-bound and unchanged.

hard_gates.name: failure-coverage
hard_gates.evidence: All and only the 16 original answerable failures were audited.

hard_gates.name: evaluation-validity
hard_gates.evidence: All 16 public questions were non-unique but labelled answerable with one canonical range.

hard_gates.name: product-ambiguity-safety
hard_gates.evidence: The product answered all 16 cases instead of clarifying.

failures.evidence: Every failed public question permitted at least two plausible retrieved source ranges but gold required one range and answer action.
Every corrected action is clarify, but the persisted product action was answer.

decision.rationale: Do not lower the frozen gates or reinterpret the previous result as a pass. Correct reference uniqueness and product ambiguity handling together, then evaluate once on new source-disjoint evidence. No Release remains.

limitations: Semantic uniqueness was adjudicated by Codex rather than an independent external human.
The 96.8% overall and 86.21% boundary action sensitivity values are diagnostic only and do not replace official metrics.
The audit uses already opened public-source development evidence and supports no fresh confirmation claim.
